title: Snakebite
confirm_prompt: This sounds like a snakebite. Say go, or tap Continue, and I'll talk you through it — but call for help as soon as you can either way.
match_cues: swelling and pain after a bite
bitten on the leg or arm outdoors

steps.text: Move them away from the snake, but do not try to catch it or kill it. Keep everyone else back.
Call for help now. Antivenom is the treatment and it is only available at a hospital, so getting them there quickly matters more than anything you do here.
Keep them as still and as calm as you can. Movement moves venom through the body faster. Do not let them walk if you can avoid it.
Keep the bitten limb still, and level with or below the heart. Support it with a splint or a sling if you have one.
Take off any rings, watches, bracelets or tight clothing near the bite, before it swells.
Do not cut the bite. Do not try to suck the venom out. Do not apply ice, and do not tie a tourniquet. All of these cause harm.
If you can do it safely from where you are, note the time of the bite and what the snake looked like. Do not go looking for it.
Stay with them and keep watching their breathing. If they stop responding or stop breathing normally, tell me straight away.

sources: World Health Organization, Guidelines for the Management of Snakebites (2nd edition) — First aid and transport to hospital
World Health Organization, Snakebite envenoming fact sheet
International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020 — Snakebite
